domain_label: Question Craft & Answering — Exam Item Typology (INBDE formats + Patient Box, TOEFL 2026 & legacy task types, per-item time budget)
purpose: A method for classifying the exam item a study-system learner is facing and routing it to the right answering playbook and time budget: identify the exam (INBDE vs TOEFL) and its format before choosing any tactic; enumerate the INBDE's one-best-answer standalone/itemset/case formats and the Patient Box, and hold the negative finding that the INBDE uses no multiple-response/ordering/hotspot items; enumerate the TOEFL iBT 2026 per-section task types and the legacy 2023-2025 types that still fill prep banks; set the per-item-type timing budget; and refuse to apply a format's tactic (e.g. select-all elimination) to an exam that lacks that format. Every INBDE/TOEFL structural fact is drawn from the official JCNDE and ETS pages cited in the research file but was verified this session via search-engine excerpts quoting those pages (direct fetch returned 403 through the sandbox proxy), so FACT tags name the source and carry that verification caveat; prep-triangulated numbers are ESTIMATE and the one open pretest-format question is held UNKNOWN.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the two target exams are the INBDE (US dental board for foreign graduates, JCNDE/ADA) and the TOEFL iBT in its 2026-01-21 format, per the sibling research files exam_dental_us_fmg.md and exam_toefl.md

every INBDE/TOEFL FACT was verified via search-engine excerpts quoting the named official JCNDE/ETS page, NOT by reading the page body, because the sandbox egress proxy denied CONNECT (403) to jcnde.ada.org, nbme.org and ets.org this session; the official URLs are cited so a fetch-enabled run can confirm verbatim
per-item time budgets are prep-site-triangulated ESTIMATEs consistent with the official item totals and section times, not official per-type stopwatch figures
answering-strategy content is craft synthesized from the NBME flaw taxonomy and the structural facts, marked ESTIMATE, not an official rubric
exclusions: the NBME item-WRITING canon (cover-the-options construction, the two flaw families, homogeneous options) beyond naming the cover-the-options rule as the basis of the answer-before-looking move — that item-authoring KB is a separate specialist
Bloom-level tagging and how item format bounds the assessable cognitive process — a separate item-classification concern
psychometric item statistics (difficulty p-value, point-biserial, discrimination index, IRT b/a/c, distractor analysis) and question-bank metadata schema — the CTT/IRT bank-metadata KB

the INBDE two-axis content blueprint (Foundation Knowledge x Clinical Content, the 56 clinical content items whose enumeration is pending official-PDF access) and TOEFL scoring-band interpretation beyond the one INBDE scaled-score fact
subject-matter dental or English content of any item; this KB is about item FORMAT and answering procedure, not the answers

competency_questions.question: What item formats does the INBDE actually use, and what property do all of them share?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states the INBDE relies exclusively on multiple-choice items, that every item is one-best-answer with 3-5 options, and that items are either standalone or grouped, citing the JCNDE Item Development / Candidate Guides as FACT (verified via search excerpt)

competency_questions.question: What is the Patient Box and how does it relate to standalones, itemsets and cases?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: defines the Patient Box as the standardized patient-summary table usable with standalones or sets and shows the itemset uses the Patient Box alone while the case adds an image/stimulus

competency_questions.question: How do INBDE itemsets and cases differ, and how many items does each group carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states both are groups of 3-6 items and the difference is the stimulus: itemset = Patient Box only, case = Patient Box plus an image or other stimulus (radiograph, photo, chart)

competency_questions.question: Does the INBDE use select-all-that-apply, ordering, drag-and-drop or hotspot items, and what remains unknown?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: reports the negative finding that no multiple-response/ordering/drag-drop/hotspot format was found and the guide language excludes them, and names the residual UNKNOWN of whether unscored pretest items ever pilot other formats

competency_questions.question: Is there a fixed ratio of standalone items to item sets on the INBDE?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states there is no predetermined number or percentage of standalones vs sets and that test-construction teams pick whichever format best tests the concept, as FACT

competency_questions.question: What changed in the TOEFL iBT on 2026-01-21?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states the 2026-01-21 format change to a section-adaptive ~90-minute test with 1-6 band scores that dropped the legacy integrated tasks and the essay, as FACT

competency_questions.question: What are the 2026 TOEFL Reading and Listening task types?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: enumerates Reading (Complete the Words, Read in Daily Life, Read an Academic Passage) and Listening (Listen and Choose a Response, Listen to a Conversation, Listen to an Announcement, Academic Talk) with their mechanics

competency_questions.question: What are the 2026 TOEFL Speaking and Writing task types?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: enumerates Speaking (Listen and Repeat, Take an Interview) and Writing (Build a Sentence, Write an Email, Writing for an Academic Discussion) with their mechanics

competency_questions.question: Which legacy TOEFL question types still dominate published prep banks, and why do they still matter?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: lists the legacy 2023-2025 Reading/Listening/Speaking/Writing types (including prose summary select-3-of-6 and integrated tasks), marks them ESTIMATE, and notes they still fill most prep material even though the 2026 test dropped them

competency_questions.question: Where does a multiple-response format appear across the two exams, and why does the asymmetry matter for strategy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: shows legacy TOEFL DID use multiple-response and table formats (prose summary 3-of-6) while the INBDE does not, and concludes a specialist must key strategy to the format actually in front of the learner

competency_questions.question: What is the per-item time budget for each INBDE and TOEFL item type?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives the INBDE ~63s standalone and ~90-105s case-item budgets and the TOEFL budgets (Reading academic ~1 min/q, Complete the Words ~10s/blank, Listen and Choose one hearing, WAD ~10 min), flags them ESTIMATE derived from official counts/times, and notes no INBDE guessing penalty

competency_questions.question: How should a learner read a single-best-answer stem, work a case cluster, and approach a TOEFL productive task?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives the stem procedure (lead-in first, answer-before-looking, elimination, negative-stem rewrite, never leave blanks), the case-cluster procedure (scan the Patient Box once, items independently scored, do not revise for consistency), and the productive-task templates (WAD, Write an Email, legacy integrated grid, Listen and Repeat), all tagged craft/ESTIMATE

competency_questions.question: Given an arbitrary item, how do you route it to the correct format, strategy and time budget without misapplying a tactic from another format?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: identifies exam then format then stimulus, selects the matching playbook and time budget, and refuses to apply a format-specific tactic (e.g. select-all elimination or an integrated-task template) to an exam/format that lacks it

glossary.definition: An item with 3-5 answer choices rankable on a single dimension where only one option is considered the correct or best answer; per the INBDE Candidate Guide this is the INBDE's only item format [FACT, verified via search excerpt of jcnde.ada.org guides].
An INBDE multiple-choice item presented in isolation, not attached to a shared set of stimuli; the counterpart to grouped item sets [FACT - INBDE Item Development Guide].

The INBDE's standardized patient-summary table (demographics, chief complaint, history, findings) that can accompany a standalone or a set; the guide says it enables direct skill assessment while avoiding unnecessary verbiage — the NBME clinical vignette made into a fixed template [FACT].
An INBDE group of 3-6 items associated with a Patient Box only (no image) [FACT - INBDE Item Development Guide via search excerpt].
An INBDE group of 3-6 items associated with a Patient Box PLUS an image or other stimulus such as a radiograph, photograph or chart [FACT - INBDE Item Development Guide via search excerpt].

A 'select all that apply' format with more than one keyed correct option; present in legacy TOEFL (e.g. the prose-summary select-3-of-6 task and some Listening table items) but ABSENT from the INBDE, whose guide language excludes it [FACT negative finding].

The 2026 TOEFL iBT property whereby a section's later (stage-2) module difficulty depends on stage-1 performance, so exact per-type item counts vary between test-takers [FACT for adaptivity; ESTIMATE that this is why per-type counts vary].

The 2026 TOEFL Writing task: respond to a professor's discussion prompt plus two classmate posts, ~10 minutes, >=100 words recommended, scored on relevant contribution [FACT for the task; ESTIMATE for the internal time split].

The 2023-2025 TOEFL task set (integrated read-listen tasks, the independent essay, multi-response reading such as prose summary) that the 2026 test dropped but that still dominates published prep banks; practice material must be labeled legacy vs current [FACT that it was dropped; ESTIMATE for the full legacy taxonomy].

The NBME item-writing principle that a properly focused lead-in lets a test-taker read the vignette and lead-in, cover the options, and produce the answer unaided; inverted by the learner into the 'answer before looking' solving move that immunizes against engineered distractors [FACT for the rule; ESTIMATE for the tactic].

The working seconds-per-item allotment for a format (e.g. ~63s INBDE standalone, ~90-105s INBDE case item, ~1 min TOEFL academic-reading question, ~10 min WAD), derived from official item counts and section times and used to pace a first pass and a flag-and-move threshold [ESTIMATE].

nodes.definition: Establish the governing move of the whole KB: before choosing any answering tactic, identify WHICH exam the item belongs to (INBDE vs TOEFL iBT) and WHICH format within it, because the two exams differ in ways that make a single universal MCQ playbook wrong — most sharply, the INBDE uses no multiple-response format while legacy TOEFL does. This node is the root the item-typology tree hangs from: exam identity decides the format inventory, the format decides the stimulus handling, and only then does a strategy and a time budget follow. It also carries the sourcing honesty for the tree: the structural facts below come from the official JCNDE and ETS pages named in the research file but were verified this session via search-engine excerpts quoting those pages, because the sandbox proxy returned 403 on direct fetch — so a FACT here means 'the named official page states this, confirmed by excerpt', not 'read from the page body'.

included: the exam-then-format-then-stimulus-then-strategy ordering
why a universal MCQ playbook fails across INBDE and TOEFL
the search-excerpt verification caveat on every downstream FACT
excluded: the per-format detail of either exam

pros.claim: Fixing the exam and format first stops a tactic learned on one exam from misfiring on another
pros.example: not applying legacy-TOEFL select-all elimination to an INBDE one-best-answer item

cons.claim: The identity step adds a gate before answering that a rushed learner may skip on a familiar-looking item

treating a FACT as read from the official page when it was only confirmed via a search excerpt

nodes.definition: State the INBDE's single item model: the exam relies EXCLUSIVELY on multiple-choice items and every item is one-best-answer — 'only one of the responses is considered the correct, or best option' — with 3 to 5 answer choices per item [FACT - INBDE Candidate Guide and Item Development Guide, jcnde.ada.org, via search excerpt]. One-best-answer means the options are rankable on a single dimension and exactly one is defensibly best, so the solving move is to find the single best option, never to select a subset. This model is what every INBDE format (standalone, itemset, case) instantiates, and it is the property that most distinguishes the INBDE from legacy TOEFL, which carried true multiple-response tasks.

included: the exclusively-multiple-choice, one-best-answer, 3-5-option facts
the single-best (not subset) solving implication
that all INBDE formats instantiate this model

pros.claim: A single confirmed item model lets every INBDE tactic assume exactly one best answer among 3-5 options
pros.example: predicting one answer and matching it rather than weighing which combination of options is correct

cons.claim: The '3 to 5 options' range is a stated band, so option count is not fixed and a tactic keyed to a fixed count is brittle
cons.example: assuming always four options and mis-estimating elimination odds on a three-option item

failure_modes: treating an INBDE item as if more than one option could be keyed
assuming a fixed option count instead of the stated 3-5 range
acceptance_tests: the model is stated as exclusively multiple-choice, one-best-answer, 3-5 options, cited to the JCNDE guides as FACT (via search excerpt), with the single-best solving implication

nodes.definition: Model the standalone item: an INBDE one-best-answer MCQ 'presented in isolation', not attached to a shared set of stimuli [FACT - INBDE Item Development Guide via search excerpt]. It is the atomic INBDE format; a standalone may still be accompanied by a Patient Box (the standardized patient-summary table can be used with standalones as well as sets), but it is scored on its own with no cross-item shared stimulus. Standalones dominate Day 1 sections 1-3 (~100 items each) in the delivery structure and are answered at the fastest per-item pace (~63s), so the standalone is both the default classification and the timing baseline the other formats are measured against.

pros.example: answering a Day-1 standalone in ~63s rather than treating it as part of a set

cons.claim: A standalone can still carry a Patient Box, so 'has a patient table' does not by itself mean it is a set
cons.example: mistaking a standalone-with-Patient-Box for the first item of a case

nodes.definition: Model the Patient Box: a standardized patient-summary table (demographics, chief complaint, history, findings) that the INBDE attaches to items; the Item Development Guide says it exists to enable direct skill assessment while 'avoiding unnecessary verbiage' [FACT - INBDE Item Development Guide via search excerpt]. It is the same idea as the NBME clinical vignette (age/sex/site -> chief complaint -> history -> exam -> labs/imaging) but rendered as a fixed template. Crucially it is usable with standalones AS WELL AS sets, so the Patient Box is a stimulus TYPE, not itself a grouping; it is the shared spine of the itemset and case formats and the artifact the case-cluster answering tactic scans once up front.

nodes.definition: Model the itemset: an INBDE group of 3-6 items associated with a Patient Box ONLY (no image) [FACT - INBDE Item Development Guide via search excerpt]. Every item in the set is still a one-best-answer MCQ; the set shares only the patient-summary table, and the items are independently scored so one item is not meant to reveal another's answer. The itemset is the lighter of the two grouped formats — it differs from the case exactly by the absence of an added image/stimulus — and it inherits the case-cluster answering discipline: scan the Patient Box once, then answer each item at close to standalone speed.

nodes.definition: Model the case: an INBDE group of 3-6 items associated with a Patient Box PLUS an image or other stimulus — a radiograph, photograph or chart [FACT - INBDE Item Development Guide via search excerpt]. It is the richer grouped format: the items are still independently scored one-best-answer MCQs, but the shared stimulus now includes visual material the learner must orient to (film type, region) before reading the items. Cases populate Day 1 section 4 (~60 items, ~105s/item) and Day 2 (~70 items/section, ~90s/item) in the delivery structure, so the case carries the highest per-item time budget because the shared image warrants front-loaded interpretation amortized across the set.

nodes.definition: Record the mix rule: the INBDE does not at present contain a predetermined number or percentage of items allocated to standalones as opposed to item sets — test-construction teams pick whichever format best tests the concept [FACT - INBDE Item Development Guide via search excerpt]. The consequence for a study system is that no reliable ratio of standalones to sets can be assumed or drilled to; a learner must be format-agile rather than expecting a fixed proportion. This bounds the router: it classifies each item as it comes rather than predicting the session's format distribution.

nodes.definition: Model the INBDE delivery structure and the per-item seconds it implies: Day 1 sections 1-3 are ~100 standalone items each (300) at 105 min/section (~63s/item); Day 1 section 4 is ~60 case-based items at 105 min (~105s/item); Day 2 sections 1-2 are ~70 case-based items each (140) at 105 min/section (~90s/item) [ESTIMATE - high confidence; the section table is triangulated from prep-site readings of the Candidate Guide, consistent with the official 500-item total]. Two scoring facts frame the pace: there is NO penalty for guessing, and the result is a scaled score 49-99 with pass = 75 that is NOT 75% correct (scaling accounts for item difficulty, discrimination and guessing) [FACT - JCNDE results/scoring FAQ via search excerpt]. Optional 15-min breaks sit between sections; unscheduled breaks run the clock.

nodes.definition: Give the single-best-answer stem procedure for an INBDE standalone [ESTIMATE - craft, medium-high; synthesized from the NBME flaw taxonomy and the structural facts]: (1) read the lead-in (last line) first, then the vignette, so you know what data matters — for short stems straight-through is fine; (2) answer before looking (the cover-the-options rule inverted into a solving move): commit to a predicted answer then find its match, immunizing against distractors engineered to be plausible; (3) if no prediction is possible, eliminate — strike options that are true but non-responsive to the lead-in, internally false, or heterogeneous with the others, using writer flaws (absolute-term options usually wrong, the odd-one-out grammatically usually wrong) only as tiebreakers; (4) rewrite a negative/EXCEPT stem mentally as 'mark each option true/false, pick the false one'; (5) never leave blanks — the INBDE has no guessing penalty [FACT], and TOEFL MC has no documented penalty [ESTIMATE - none seen].

nodes.definition: Compose the router the whole KB builds toward: given an arbitrary item, classify it exam -> format -> stimulus -> strategy -> time budget and emit a go/no-go on applying a tactic. Steps: (1) identify the exam (INBDE vs TOEFL) and, for TOEFL, the era (2026 vs legacy); (2) classify the format — INBDE standalone / itemset / case, or the specific TOEFL task type; (3) read the stimulus type (none / Patient Box / image / audio); (4) select the matching playbook via the format-match rule (stem procedure, case-cluster procedure, or productive template); (5) attach the per-item time budget. It refuses these mismatches as no-go: applying select-all/partial-credit reasoning to any INBDE item (no multiple-response exists), using an integrated-task template on a 2026 TOEFL item (integrated tasks were dropped), asserting a fixed standalone-vs-set ratio (none is predetermined), leaving a blank under a no-penalty regime, and treating a search-excerpt FACT as verbatim official reading. Since no INBDE/TOEFL page was directly fetchable this session, the router marks every structural FACT with its verification path and every pretest-format claim as UNKNOWN.

conflict_axes.name: universal_playbook_vs_exam_format_identity
conflict_axes.description: The pull to run one universal MCQ playbook versus first identifying the exam and format, which differ enough (INBDE has no multiple-response; TOEFL split into 2026 vs legacy) that a universal playbook misfires.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always resolve exam -> format -> stimulus before choosing a tactic; the format in front selects the playbook

conflict_axes.name: one_best_answer_vs_multiple_response_habit
conflict_axes.description: The INBDE's exclusively one-best-answer model pulls against a select-all/partial-credit habit carried from legacy TOEFL or other exams.
poles: solve for the single best of 3-5 options
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: restrict multiple-response reasoning to legacy-TOEFL multi-response items; every INBDE item has exactly one best answer

conflict_axes.name: predict_then_match_vs_eliminate
conflict_axes.description: On a single-best-answer stem the answer-before-looking prediction move competes with an options-first elimination pass.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: predict and match first to immunize against distractors, and fall back to elimination only when no prediction is possible

conflict_axes.name: lead_in_first_vs_read_straight_through
conflict_axes.description: Reading the lead-in before the vignette targets the relevant data but adds a step that is wasted on short stems where straight-through reading is faster.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read the lead-in first on long vignette stems; read straight through on short stems

conflict_axes.name: front_load_stimulus_vs_reread_per_item
conflict_axes.description: Scanning the Patient Box and image once up front competes with rereading the shared stimulus for each item in a set.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: scan the Patient Box and orient to the image once, then treat them as a lookup table per item

conflict_axes.name: consistency_pressure_vs_independent_scoring
conflict_axes.description: The urge to keep a set's answers internally consistent competes with the fact that set items are independently scored and non-cascading.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer each item on its own evidence and never revise an earlier answer merely to match a later item

conflict_axes.name: current_2026_material_vs_legacy_prep_banks

poles: practice the abundant legacy banks as-is
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tag every practice item current vs legacy and prep the 2026 test on current tasks, mining legacy banks only for transferable skills

conflict_axes.name: speed_vs_accuracy_within_time_budget
conflict_axes.description: The per-item time budget pulls toward moving on while accuracy pulls toward verifying, especially where a set shares one section clock.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the first-pass budget and flag-and-move at the threshold, banking any set surplus on the shared stimulus rather than on re-checking single items

edge_cases.trigger: a scaled score misread as a percentage
edge_cases.mitigation: the scaled 49-99 scale (pass 75) accounts for item difficulty, discrimination and guessing; a scaled 75 is not 75% correct

edge_cases.description: A Complete the Words item is treated as full-word vocabulary recall
edge_cases.trigger: misreading the C-test mechanic where only the second half of each word's letters is deleted
edge_cases.mitigation: only the second half of the letters is missing and the first sentence is intact; use the intact sentence to fix the topic and spend ~10s/blank

edge_cases.description: A WAD response is written under length or off-prompt
edge_cases.trigger: a timed productive task rushed without a template
edge_cases.mitigation: use the WAD template: take a clear position, give a reason plus example, engage a classmate by name, and reach >=100 words within ~10 minutes

workflow.action: Identify the exam and format in front of the learner
workflow.description: Determine INBDE vs TOEFL and, for TOEFL, the 2026-vs-legacy era, before any tactic
workflow.gate: the exam, then the format, then the stimulus are named before a tactic, with the search-excerpt verification caveat noted

workflow.action: Confirm the one-best-answer model and option count
workflow.description: Confirm an INBDE item is exclusively one-best-answer with 3-5 options
workflow.gate: the item is confirmed one-best-answer (single best of 3-5), cited FACT via search excerpt

workflow.action: Classify the INBDE item as standalone or a Patient-Box set
workflow.description: Decide whether the item is isolated or part of a group sharing a Patient Box
workflow.gate: the item is classified isolated or grouped, noting a standalone may still carry a Patient Box

workflow.action: Distinguish itemset from case by the stimulus
workflow.description: For a set, decide itemset (Patient Box only) vs case (Patient Box plus image)
workflow.gate: the set is labeled itemset or case by presence of an added image, both 3-6 items

workflow.description: Rule out multiple-response/ordering/drag-drop/hotspot and note the pretest UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: no multiple-response/ordering/hotspot format is assumed and the pretest-format residual is held [UNKNOWN]

workflow.action: Map the TOEFL section to its 2026 task type
workflow.gate: the TOEFL item is mapped to a named 2026 task with its mechanics and item format

workflow.action: Flag legacy versus current TOEFL material
workflow.description: Tag whether the item is a current 2026 task or a legacy 2023-2025 type
workflow.gate: the item is tagged current or legacy, with legacy types marked ESTIMATE

workflow.description: Note where multiple-response applies (legacy TOEFL) and where it does not (INBDE)
workflow.gate: multi-response tactics are scoped to legacy-TOEFL items only and excluded from every INBDE item

workflow.description: Attach the per-item-type second/minute budget and flag-and-move threshold
workflow.gate: the item carries its ESTIMATE budget (e.g. ~63s standalone, ~105s case item, ~10 min WAD) with a flag-and-move rule

workflow.description: Run the stem, case-cluster or productive-template procedure the format selects
workflow.gate: the playbook matches the classified format (stem / case-cluster / productive template), never a mismatched one

workflow.action: Route and gate the format, strategy and budget into a verdict
workflow.description: Emit the exam->format->stimulus->strategy->budget verdict and refuse mismatched tactics
workflow.gate: the verdict runs the full pipeline, refuses the enumerated mismatches, and carries the FACT-verification-path and UNKNOWN-pretest caveats

dominance_rules.rule: The exam+format identity dominates any generic MCQ tactic
dominance_rules.rationale: the INBDE and TOEFL differ enough (no INBDE multiple-response; TOEFL 2026 vs legacy) that a tactic chosen before the format is known can be simply inapplicable
dominance_rules.trigger: a tactic is selected before the exam and format are identified
dominance_rules.action: resolve exam -> format -> stimulus first and let the format select the tactic

dominance_rules.rule: INBDE one-best-answer dominates any multiple-response habit
dominance_rules.rationale: the INBDE is exclusively one-best-answer and has no select-all/ordering/hotspot format
dominance_rules.trigger: select-all elimination or partial-credit reasoning is applied to an INBDE item
dominance_rules.action: solve for the single best of the 3-5 options and drop the multi-response tactic

dominance_rules.rule: The current 2026 TOEFL format dominates legacy prep material for a 2026 test-taker
dominance_rules.rationale: the 2026 test dropped the integrated tasks and the essay that still fill legacy banks
dominance_rules.trigger: legacy integrated-task or essay practice is used to prep the 2026 test
dominance_rules.action: prep on the current 2026 task types and mine legacy material only for transferable skill

dominance_rules.rule: The scanned-once Patient Box dominates per-item rereading
dominance_rules.rationale: the box is a fixed lookup table and the set shares one section clock
dominance_rules.trigger: the Patient Box or shared image is reread on each item of a set
dominance_rules.action: scan the box and orient to the image once, then treat them as a lookup table per item

dominance_rules.rule: Independent scoring dominates cross-item consistency pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: set items are independently scored and written so one does not reveal another's answer
dominance_rules.trigger: an earlier set answer is revised to match a later item
dominance_rules.action: answer each item on its own evidence and never cascade a revision across the set

dominance_rules.rationale: the INBDE has no penalty for guessing and no TOEFL MC penalty is documented
dominance_rules.trigger: an item is about to be left blank
dominance_rules.action: always mark an answer, flag-and-move rather than skip

dominance_rules.rule: The lead-in dominates the vignette on read order for long stems
dominance_rules.rationale: knowing the question first tells the reader which vignette data matters
dominance_rules.trigger: a long vignette stem is being read
dominance_rules.action: read the lead-in first, then the vignette; read straight through only on short stems

dominance_rules.rule: The task inventory dominates the exact per-type item count
dominance_rules.rationale: the 2026 test is section-adaptive so per-type counts vary between test-takers
dominance_rules.trigger: practice is planned by a fixed number of each 2026 task
dominance_rules.action: plan by task type and its time budget, not by a fixed per-type count

dominance_rules.rule: Search-excerpt sourcing dominates a claim of verbatim official reading
dominance_rules.rationale: the official JCNDE/ETS pages were 403-blocked this session and confirmed only via excerpts
dominance_rules.trigger: a structural FACT is presented as read verbatim from the official page
dominance_rules.action: state the FACT was verified via a search excerpt of the cited page and re-verify on direct-fetch access

anti_rework_rules.rule: Identify the exam and format before drilling any answering strategy
anti_rework_rules.prevents: learning a tactic that misfires on the actual format and having to unlearn it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every practice item current-2026 or legacy before using it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: prepping dropped integrated/essay tasks for the 2026 test and wasting practice time

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the INBDE item is one-best-answer before applying elimination
anti_rework_rules.prevents: multiple-response habits corrupting single-best reasoning across a whole practice set

anti_rework_rules.rule: Scan the Patient Box once, up front, before item 1 of a set
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rereading the box per item and overrunning the shared section clock

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the per-item time budget before the first pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spending case-item time on standalones and running out of section clock late

anti_rework_rules.rule: Mark an answer on every item as you go
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a scramble to fill blanks at the end under a no-guessing-penalty regime

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label each structural FACT with its verification path when first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a search-excerpt claim circulating as verbatim-verified and being retracted after a direct-fetch check

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the pretest-format question as UNKNOWN rather than asserting the exclusion is absolute
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invented certainty about pretest items that a later official PDF could contradict

iteration_protocol.trigger: the official JCNDE Item Development Guide or Candidate Guide becomes directly fetchable
iteration_protocol.action: verify the standalone/itemset/case definitions, item-count ranges and format exclusions verbatim and lift the search-excerpt caveat where confirmed

iteration_protocol.trigger: the ETS TOEFL content and sample-test pages become directly fetchable
iteration_protocol.action: confirm the 2026 task-type enumeration and per-type mechanics verbatim and lift the search-excerpt caveat where confirmed

iteration_protocol.trigger: an official INBDE section-level timing table is obtained
iteration_protocol.action: replace the prep-triangulated per-item second estimates with the official section counts and times

iteration_protocol.trigger: it becomes known whether unscored INBDE pretest items pilot other formats
iteration_protocol.action: resolve the [UNKNOWN] residual and update the format-exclusion statement accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: ETS documents a TOEFL wrong-answer penalty or explicitly confirms none
iteration_protocol.action: update the never-leave-blanks rule and the pacing for TOEFL items

iteration_protocol.trigger: the adaptive stage-2 module's per-type item counts are published
iteration_protocol.action: replace the 'counts vary' estimate with the published ranges

iteration_protocol.trigger: a learner-facing question bank tags items by format
iteration_protocol.action: align the router's format taxonomy and no-go rules to the bank's tags

iteration_protocol.trigger: legacy TOEFL material is retired from the prep bank
iteration_protocol.action: retire the legacy note-grid template and de-emphasize the multiple-response asymmetry handling

priority_rationale: The exam-then-format identity root and the INBDE one-best-answer model come first because every classification and tactic depends on knowing which exam and format an item belongs to; the INBDE formats (standalone, Patient Box, itemset, case), their exclusions and no-fixed-ratio rule, and the TOEFL 2026 task types plus legacy taxonomy come next because they are the item inventory the router draws from; the multiple-response asymmetry and the delivery-timing and per-item budget follow because they turn the inventory into strategy-relevant distinctions and pacing; the stem, case-cluster and productive-template procedures then attach a playbook to each format; and the format-match rule and the router come last because they compose every upstream classification, budget and tactic into a mismatch-refusing per-item verdict.
